items.jp: 此処に座ってもいいですか
items.kana: ここにすわってもいいですか

structure_explanation.en: Here appears the permission-asking pattern 「verb in te-form + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = may sit / it's okay to sit). 此処に marks the place where one wants to sit, 座って is the te-form of the verb, も adds the sense of "even (if)", and いいですか politely asks whether it is okay. Together it becomes the polite request "may I sit here?".
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Aqui aparece o padrão de pedir permissão 「verbo na forma て + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = pode sentar / está ok sentar). O 此処に marca o lugar onde se quer sentar, 座って é a forma て do verbo, も acrescenta o sentido de "mesmo (se)", e いいですか pergunta educadamente se está tudo bem. O conjunto vira o pedido cortês "posso me sentar aqui?".

translation_literal.en: As for sitting here, is it okay (to do so)?
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a sentar-se aqui, mesmo (que seja) está bom?

conjugation_note.en: て-form of 座る (座っ + て)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma て de 座る (座っ + て)

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form (present) of いい, within 〜てもいい
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (presente) de いい, dentro de 〜てもいい

findings.issue: Generated JP writes ここ with the literary/dated kanji 此処. Modern native writing and all JLPT-oriented material use kana ここ; 此処 is unnatural orthography for a learner sentence.
findings.current: 此処に座ってもいいですか
findings.proposed: jp: ここに座ってもいいですか — also update tokens[0].s from 此処 to ここ and replace 此処に with ここに in expl_en and expl_pt, which cite the old orthography.

items.jp: １日から新しい仕事が始まる
items.kana: いちにちからあたらしいしごとがはじまる

structure_explanation.en: The time expression １日から (from the 1st) opens the sentence, followed by the subject 新しい仕事 (new job) marked by が, and the intransitive verb 始まる (to begin). The verb is intransitive: the thing 'begins on its own', without anyone who starts it. The focus is the vocabulary and the reading of the number/date.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A expressão de tempo １日から (a partir do dia 1) abre a frase, seguida do sujeito 新しい仕事 (trabalho novo) marcado por が, e do verbo intransitivo 始まる (começar). O verbo é intransitivo: a coisa 'começa por si', sem alguém que a inicie. O foco é o vocabulário e a leitura do número/data.

translation_literal.en: From the 1st, a new job begins.
translation_literal.pt-BR: A partir do dia 1, trabalho novo começa.

translation.en: The new job starts on the 1st.
translation.pt-BR: O trabalho novo começa no dia 1.

role.en: time noun (part of the date: the 1st)
role.pt-BR: substantivo de tempo (parte da data: dia 1)

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of 新しい (い-adjective)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 新しい (い-adjetivo)

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of 始まる (intransitive verb), present/future
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 始まる (verbo intransitivo), presente/futuro

findings.issue: Tokens １ (r=いち) and 日 (r=にち) give the wrong reading for the date sense. ついたち is a fused reading and cannot be split as いち+にち; the two tokens should be merged into one token １日 read ついたち.
findings.proposed: merge into one token s=１日, r=ついたち (fused date reading 'the 1st')

items.jp: 彼は正しい、尤も少し厳しいです
items.kana: かれわただしい、もっともすこしきびしいです

structure_explanation.en: The topic 彼 (he) is marked by は and takes the i-adjective 正しい (correct/right) as its predicate. After the comma, 尤も (mottomo) introduces a caveat ('though', 'it is true that'). The second part 少し厳しいです uses the adverb 少し (a little) + the i-adjective 厳しい (strict) + polite です. Note the slight mix of register (正しい without です, then です at the end), common in more casual written Japanese.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico 彼 (ele) é marcado por は e recebe como predicado o adjetivo い 正しい (correto/ter razão). Após a vírgula, 尤も (mottomo) introduz uma ressalva ('embora', 'é verdade que'). A segunda parte 少し厳しいです usa o advérbio 少し (um pouco) + o adjetivo い 厳しい (severo) + です polido. Observe a leve mistura de registro (正しい sem です, depois です no fim), comum em japonês escrito mais solto.

translation_literal.en: As for him, (he is) correct; it is true, but, (that he is) a little strict.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a ele, (está) correto; é verdade, porém, (que é) um pouco severo.

translation.en: He's right, even if he's a bit harsh.
translation.pt-BR: Ele tem razão, embora seja um pouco severo.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of 正しい (い-adjective)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 正しい (adjetivo い)

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of 厳しい (い-adjective)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 厳しい (adjetivo い)

conjugation_note.en: です attached to 厳しい only for politeness
conjugation_note.pt-BR: です anexado a 厳しい apenas para polidez

findings.issue: Generated JP is unnatural: comma splice joining a plain predicate (正しい) to a polite one (です) in one sentence, and the concessive 尤も normally starts a new clause/sentence with the caveat ending in が. The expl's claim that this mix is 'common' papers over the defect.
findings.current: 彼は正しい、尤も少し厳しいです
findings.proposed: 彼は正しい。尤も、少し厳しいが — consistent plain register, drop the trailing 。 per GENERATED-jp convention (or fully polite: 彼は正しいです。尤も、少し厳しいですが). Cascade kana/romaji/tokens/expl.

items.jp: 教室にだれもいません
items.kana: きょうしつにだれもいません

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the pattern だれも + negative verb, which means nobody. に marks the place (the classroom) where existence is checked, and いません is the polite negative form of いる (to exist, for animate beings). The combination だれも...いません expresses the total absence of people. When も joins an interrogative (だれ) in a negative predicate, the meaning becomes nobody.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão だれも + verbo negativo, que significa ninguém. に marca o lugar (a sala de aula) onde se verifica a existência, e いません é a forma negativa polida de いる (existir, para seres animados). A combinação だれも...いません expressa a ausência total de pessoas. Quando も se junta a um interrogativo (だれ) num predicado negativo, o sentido vira ninguém.

translation_literal.en: In the classroom (に), no one (だれも) is there (いません), polite negative.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Na sala de aula (に), ninguém (だれも), não há/não está (いません), polido negativo.

translation.en: There's no one in the classroom.
translation.pt-BR: Não tem ninguém na sala de aula.

gloss.en: who (here: no one, with も + negative)

role.en: interrogative pronoun (becomes 'nobody' in the だれも + negative pattern)
role.pt-BR: pronome interrogativo (vira 'ninguém' no padrão だれも + negativo)

conjugation_note.en: い = connective stem of いる, base for the polite negation ません
conjugation_note.pt-BR: い = raiz conetiva de いる, base para a negação polida ません

conjugation_note.en: ませ = form of ます used before ん; ません = polite negative
conjugation_note.pt-BR: ませ = forma de ます usada antes de ん; ません = negativo polido

conjugation_note.en: ん (from ぬ) completes the polite negation ません
conjugation_note.pt-BR: ん (de ぬ) completa a negação polida ません

findings.issue: In the pt-BR note of token い ('raiz conetiva de いる...'): 'conetiva' is European-Portuguese (AO90 pt-PT) spelling; Brazilian Portuguese keeps the c: 'conectiva'.
findings.current: い = raiz conetiva de いる, base para a negação polida ません
findings.proposed: い = raiz conectiva de いる, base para a negação polida ません

items.kana: くるまをちゅうしゃじょうにとめた

structure_explanation.en: The structure follows the basic Japanese order: object + verb at the end. 車を marks the car as the direct object (を), 駐車場に indicates the place where the thing comes to rest (に of destination/endpoint), and 止めた is the verb 止める ('to stop/to park something') in the past. Note the use of に (and not で) because the focus is on the point where the car ends up parked.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura segue a ordem básica do japonês: objeto + verbo no fim. 車を marca o carro como objeto direto (を), 駐車場に indica o lugar onde a coisa fica parada (に de destino/ponto final), e 止めた é o verbo 止める ('parar/estacionar algo') no passado. Note o uso de に (e não で) porque o foco é o ponto onde o carro acaba estacionado.

translation_literal.en: As for the car (を), in the parking lot (に), I parked (止めた).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao carro (を), no estacionamento (に), parei/estacionei (止めた).

translation.en: I parked the car in the parking lot.

conjugation_note.en: connective stem of 止める (past form with た)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz conetiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)

conjugation_note.en: auxiliary た that forms the past of 止める
conjugation_note.pt-BR: auxiliar た que forma o passado de 止める

findings.issue: In the pt-BR note of token 止め ('raiz conetiva de 止める...'): 'conetiva' is European-Portuguese spelling; pt-BR requires 'conectiva'.
findings.current: raiz conetiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)
findings.proposed: raiz conectiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)

items.jp: この問題が解けない学生はない
items.kana: このもんだいがとけないがくせいわない

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the target pattern 〜ない〜はない, a double negation that affirms emphatically: 'there is no X that does not...'. First comes a relative clause この問題が解けない ('that cannot solve this problem') that qualifies the noun 学生 ('student'); then 学生は is the topic and the sentence closes with はない ('there is none'). The two negations (解けない and はない) cancel out and the final meaning is positive and emphatic: every student can solve it.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão-alvo 〜ない〜はない, uma dupla negação que afirma de forma enfática: 'não existe X que não...'. Primeiro vem uma oração relativa この問題が解けない ('que não consegue resolver este problema') que qualifica o substantivo 学生 ('estudante'); depois 学生は é o tópico e a frase fecha com はない ('não existe'). As duas negações (解けない e はない) se cancelam e o sentido final é positivo e enfático: todo estudante consegue resolvê-lo.

translation_literal.en: As for a student who can't solve this problem, there isn't one.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a estudante que não consegue resolver este problema, não existe.

translation.en: There's no student who can't solve this problem.
translation.pt-BR: Não tem estudante que não consiga resolver este problema.

role.en: head of the subject of the relative clause
role.pt-BR: núcleo do sujeito da oração relativa

conjugation_note.en: imperfective base (未然形) of 解ける, potential of 解く, connecting to ない
conjugation_note.pt-BR: base imperfectiva (未然形) de 解ける, potencial de 解く, ligando-se a ない

conjugation_note.en: negative form closing the relative clause: 'that cannot solve'
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma negativa que fecha a oração relativa: 'que não consegue resolver'

role.en: topic (noun modified by the relative clause)

gloss.en: does not exist, there is none

conjugation_note.en: adjective ない in dictionary form, negating existence
conjugation_note.pt-BR: adjetivo い ない na forma de dicionário, negando a existência

findings.issue: Negative existence of an animate noun (学生) requires いない, not ない. 〜はない with people is archaic/literary (and then usually with 者); as written the generated sentence is unnatural modern Japanese. kana, romaji, tokens and both expl fields need matching updates.
findings.current: この問題が解けない学生はない
findings.proposed: この問題が解けない学生はいない
